input.rationale: Last item before the run expires, and it promotes a fact I relied on inside an interpretation without ever recording it as knowledge: the RPC header admission rule. It is the compatibility window that makes adjacent-version mixed deployments work while excluding anything older, and it is what made the legacy-encoding precondition reachable rather than hypothetical.

knowledge.statement: Every incoming RPC is admitted only after its header's protocol version is checked twice: a message whose protocol version is outside the supported range is rejected as unsupported, and a message whose version is more than one behind the receiver's own configured protocol version is rejected as well. A receiver therefore serves messages from its own version and one version older, which is what allows adjacent-version mixed deployments during rolling upgrades, while an older sender is refused outright rather than silently misinterpreted.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to every RPC dispatched through the run loop's processRPC path in the captured revision, including append entries, vote and pre-vote requests, snapshots and the leadership-transfer message; the check is on the RPC header, so it constrains peers rather than the local configuration format.

knowledge.statement: Raft.timeoutNow performs an unconditional authority transition on the receiver: it clears the known leader, sets the state to Candidate, stores candidateFromLeadershipTransfer=true and responds with an empty TimeoutNowResponse. It never inspects the RPC header identity, the current configuration, or any term, and observes no election or heartbeat precondition before transitioning.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to every TimeoutNowRequest that passes checkRPCHeader, delivered to a server in any run state; the request carries only RPCHeader (ProtocolVersion, ID, Addr) and therefore cannot be evaluated for freshness.

knowledge.statement: While candidateFromLeadershipTransfer is set, runCandidate does not pre-vote: it calls electSelf directly, which increments the current term and sends RequestVote with LeadershipTransfer=true. The flag is cleared by a deferred store(false) when the candidate run ends.
knowledge.conditions: Set only by timeoutNow in the captured source; applies to a node that then enters/continues the candidate state.

knowledge.statement: requestVote rejects a vote request that arrives while a different leader is known, but skips that rejection when req.LeadershipTransfer is true; the older-term rejection and the log-suffix comparison still run before a vote is granted.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to RequestVoteRequest handling on any server that has a recorded leader whose address differs from the candidate and whose protocol version carries the LeadershipTransfer flag.

knowledge.statement: The other authority-bearing RPC handlers guard their state change with the sender's term: appendEntries returns early when a.Term is below the current term and only adopts/updates term and state when the request term is greater (or the receiver is not a follower), and installSnapshot ignores a snapshot whose request term is older than the current term.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to AppendEntriesRequest and InstallSnapshotRequest processing; this is the control contrast for the TimeoutNow handler, which has no term to compare.

knowledge.statement: The leader-side leadershipTransfer routine only issues the TimeoutNow RPC after it has driven the target's replication nextIndex past the leader's last log index, i.e. the producer establishes a caught-up target before transferring.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the sender path invoked from leaderLoop; it is not verified by, nor visible to, the receiving timeoutNow handler.

knowledge.statement: GetConfiguration does not read main-thread membership state: it returns a configurationsFuture whose configurations field is filled from the atomically published latestConfiguration, which is written only by setLatestConfiguration (and cleared/initialised elsewhere), so the value a client sees is whatever that atomic last held.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to any caller of GetConfiguration on any server, including followers, independent of the main-thread run loop.

knowledge.statement: Configuration log entries are not delivered to the FSM: the apply loop dispatches only LogCommand to r.fsm.Apply, and for LogConfiguration it calls ConfigurationStore.StoreConfiguration only when the FSM implements ConfigurationStore (otherwise it returns early). MockFSM therefore records only LogCommand payloads in its logs slice and never records a configuration unless the ConfigStoreFSM option is used.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to commit-application in the captured snapshot for every server, regardless of protocol version; Noop and barrier entries likewise never reach FSM.Apply.

knowledge.statement: The captured cluster test helper's EnsureSame compares FSM-applied log payloads and the FSM's recorded configuration list, and its polling limit defaults to 5 seconds (overridden only by a positive MakeClusterOpts.LongstopTimeout). Built with a plain MockFSM and without ConfigStoreFSM, both compared values are empty for a scenario whose only entries are configuration and noop entries, so EnsureSame can pass without establishing that a peer holds the configuration entry.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to clusters created through MakeCluster/MakeClusterCustom without ConfigStoreFSM; the configuration comparison is only meaningful when the FSM implements ConfigurationStore.

knowledge.statement: The appendEntries truncation path is not a mechanism for configurations.latest to stay stale: on a term conflict the conflicting entry is included in newEntries, the suffix is stored, and processConfigurationLogEntry is run for every new entry in the same call, so a configuration entry is (re)applied when it is (re)appended; when the truncated suffix really contained a configuration entry, rolling latest back to the committed configuration is the intended result.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to appendEntries handling of AppendEntriesRequest batches that clear a log suffix at or below configurations.latestIndex.

knowledge.statement: Membership changes are applied with command-specific suffrage rules: AddVoter replaces a non-voter/staging entry with a Voter and only rewrites the address of an existing Voter; AddNonvoter appends a Nonvoter when the server is absent and, when the server is already present with a different suffrage (Voter or Staging), only writes its address while keeping that suffrage; DemoteVoter is the command that turns an existing server into a Nonvoter; RemoveServer deletes the entry. A resulting configuration with no voters is rejected.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to nextConfiguration for a request whose prevIndex matches the current configuration index; the capture's table expectations record the suffrage outcome for each command and initial suffrage.

knowledge.statement: Only some committed log types reach the FSM thread: prepareLog returns a commit tuple for LogBarrier and LogCommand, and for LogConfiguration only when protocolVersion > 2. LogNoop, LogAddPeerDeprecated, LogRemovePeerDeprecated and LogConfiguration under protocol <= 2 return nil, so they never enter the FSM batch; processLogs still responds to any future attached to them from the main thread and then advances lastApplied.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to processLogs dispatching committed entries to fsmMutateCh on the leader and on followers, for every configuration of the FSM (with or without ConfigurationStore and BatchingFSM).

knowledge.statement: The FSM thread's local applied index advances for every entry it receives, except for LogConfiguration when the FSM does not implement ConfigurationStore, where the handler returns early on the stated grounds of not incrementing the index for an unimplemented operation. The index it reports in a snapshot request is that local index, so it can legitimately sit below the committed configuration index.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the single-apply path in runFSM; the batching path instead takes the index and term of the last entry in the batch whether or not it was sent to ApplyBatch.

knowledge.statement: takeSnapshot refuses to create a snapshot when the FSM-reported index is below the committed configuration index, and otherwise records that index/term together with the committed configuration and its index, then compacts only up to min(snapshot index, last log index - TrailingLogs).
knowledge.conditions: Applies to automatic and user-triggered snapshots on any server; the committed configuration is read from the main thread through configurationsCh after the FSM snapshot has been started.

knowledge.statement: A server's reported last log index is max(lastLogIndex, lastSnapshotIndex), so installing a snapshot raises the server's last index even though appendEntries and installSnapshot do not rewrite the stored log index; installSnapshot updates lastApplied, the last snapshot index, both configurations and log compaction.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to raftState.getLastIndex as used by election and replication bookkeeping and to the InstallSnapshot handler.

knowledge.statement: The automatic snapshot condition compares the log store's last index with the snapshot index using an unsigned subtraction and no ordering guard, so a log store index below the snapshot index makes the comparison permanently true.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to shouldSnapshot as invoked by the snapshot goroutine on its random SnapshotInterval; the log store index is the store's own LastIndex, not the snapshot-aware getLastIndex.

knowledge.statement: A node that recovers through InstallSnapshot while its log store keeps a lower index reports shouldSnapshot() as true indefinitely and keeps creating fresh snapshots at the installed snapshot index while completely idle: in two executions of the same fixed harness the recovered node produced 15 and 13 distinct snapshot IDs at index 202 with applied_delta 0 over a 900ms window (SnapshotInterval 40ms), while the leading node of the same cluster reported shouldSnapshot() false and exactly 1 distinct snapshot ID at index 202.
knowledge.conditions: Observed with MakeCluster(3), SnapshotInterval 40ms, SnapshotThreshold 20, TrailingLogs 5, in-memory log/snapshot stores, protocol 3, after isolating one follower, committing 140 further commands so the leader's log compacts past that follower's next index, reconnecting so the follower recovers by InstallSnapshot (log store last index stays 62, snapshot index 202), then isolating the recovered node for a 900ms window sampled every 40ms. Two executions are instances, not a universal guarantee; MonotonicLogStore implementations, production SnapshotInterval values and long-running persistence were not observed.

knowledge.statement: A verifyFuture can be woken by only one notification (vote is guarded by the notify channel being non-nil and set to nil when it fires), and every respond path is idempotent through the deferError responded flag; vote(true) only notifies once the counted votes reach quorumSize, while vote(false) notifies immediately so the leader loop can step down when any peer reports a new leader.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to VerifyLeader/verifyFuture handling in the captured revision, including the quorumSize==0 dispatch sentinel and the follower/candidate paths that reject arrivals on the shared verify channel with ErrNotLeader.

knowledge.statement: On stepping down, the leader loop responds ErrLeadershipLost to every future still in its own notify set; replication goroutines keep their notify maps separate and only clear them through notifyAll at the end of a replication RPC, so a late notification can push an already-answered verify future back onto the shared verify channel, where the next non-leader loop answers it again through the idempotent respond path.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to leadership loss (step-down, shutdown, or state change out of Leader) with outstanding VerifyLeader requests; the arrivals are handled by whichever run loop is active when they are read.

knowledge.statement: InstallSnapshot validates freshness only by term: an older term is ignored, a newer term transitions the receiver to follower and is adopted, and there is no comparison of the request's LastLogIndex with the receiver's own lastApplied, last snapshot index or log store range. On success the handler restores the FSM from the requested snapshot, sets lastApplied to the request's LastLogIndex, sets the last snapshot index to the request's LastLogIndex/LastLogTerm, replaces both the latest and committed configurations from the request, and then removes all old logs (monotonic stores) or compacts up to the request's index.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to InstallSnapshotRequest handling on any server that reaches the handler, including a server whose own applied index or snapshot index is higher than the request's; the only preceding checks in the handler are the snapshot version bounds and the term.

knowledge.statement: Recovery from a restored snapshot index depends on log replay: processLogs rejects an index at or below lastApplied, otherwise it walks from lastApplied+1 to the target index fetching each log from the store and panics when a needed entry is missing, so a restored index below the previously applied index leaves re-application to entries that must still exist in the log.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to commit-application on any server after a restore, including the install path that sets lastApplied from the request; the walk is bounded by the target commit index and sources entries either from the in-flight future map or the log store.

knowledge.statement: The sender reaches the snapshot path only when it cannot produce entries from its per-peer nextIndex, and nextIndex moves on follower responses: a rejected AppendEntries sets nextIndex to max(min(nextIndex-1, response.LastLog+1), 1), and the snapshot is opened when setupAppendEntries reports the log is not found, i.e. when the needed prefix has been compacted away.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the leader-side replication loop for each peer; the reported last log index used in the backoff comes from the follower's AppendEntriesResponse.LastLog.

knowledge.statement: Across three executions of the same isolation/compaction/reconnect probe on a 3-node in-memory cluster, the node that entered the InstallSnapshot path never reported an applied index below its own maximum: its applied index advanced 27 -> 112 -> 197 -> 257 across rounds with decrease_count 0 and applied_at_end equal to max_applied_seen, while its snapshot index (257) stayed above its surviving log store last index (197) and the two nodes that never entered the install path were monotone as well (snapshot index 257, log store last index 257, decrease_count 0).
knowledge.conditions: Observed with MakeCluster(3), SnapshotInterval 30ms, SnapshotThreshold 10, TrailingLogs 5, in-memory log/snapshot stores, protocol 3, in three rounds of 25 warm commands, isolating one follower, 60 further commands through the remaining quorum, reconnecting, and polling all nodes every 2ms for 1.2s. The probe does not construct a leader snapshot index below a follower's applied index, so this is an observed bounded result and not a guarantee for other configurations.

knowledge.statement: Pipelined replication keeps two separate cursors: pipelineSend advances a private send cursor to the last pipelined entry index + 1 as soon as the request is handed to the pipeline, while the per-follower nextIndex and the commitment map advance only from successful decoded responses (updateLastAppended stores nextIndex = last entry index + 1 and matches commitment, then notifies the verify futures as leader). The decoder aborts the pipeline on the first unsuccessful response, on a newer term (notifyAll(false) plus a step-down notification) and pipelineSend returns shouldStop when setup fails such as a compacted prefix, after which the caller falls back to standard replication or the snapshot path. setPreviousLog additionally special-cases nextIndex-1 equal to the last snapshot index so a snapshot-backed prefix is accepted as the previous log entry.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the leader-side pipeline path in the captured revision for peers that support AppendEntriesPipeline, including the fallback to replicateTo after the pipeline aborts.

knowledge.statement: An incoming AppendEntries is classified as a heartbeat by its field values on the receiving side (non-zero term, a leader address present, PrevLogEntry and PrevLogTerm zero, no entries, LeaderCommitIndex zero). When the transport has a heartbeat handler, it is invoked directly from the connection goroutine and the RPC never reaches the consumer channel; otherwise the request is dispatched to the run loop like any other RPC. The handler registered by Raft is processHeartbeat, which checks shutdown and the command type and then calls the same appendEntries handler the run loop uses.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to NetworkTransport (and to transports that implement SetHeartbeatHandler); InmemTransport declines the fast path and pushes heartbeats onto the consumer channel. The classification depends on request field values, not on an explicit RPC type.

knowledge.statement: For a heartbeat-shaped request the reachable mutations are narrow: the older-term check can return without touching state, a newer term or the sentinel condition sets the state to Follower and adopts the term, the leader address and ID are recorded, and success sets last contact; the previous-log check, the entry loop, configuration processing and the commit-index update are all skipped because PrevLogEntry is zero, there are no entries and LeaderCommitIndex is zero. Each reachable mutation goes through a synchronised accessor (atomic state or lastLock for snapshot/log indexes), leaderLock, lastContactLock, or a channel send for observer notification.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the appendEntries code path when invoked with a heartbeat-shaped request, whether by the transport fast path or the run loop; a request with entries, a non-zero PrevLogEntry or a non-zero LeaderCommitIndex takes the ordinary path and is not covered by this statement.

knowledge.statement: The leader's heartbeat goroutine sends a request carrying only the RPC header, term and leader fields, so its LeaderCommitIndex is zero; on a successful response it refreshes last contact, resets the failure count and notifies any waiting verify futures with the response's success value. Followers therefore learn the leader's commit index from the replicate loop's random CommitTimeout path rather than from heartbeats.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the leader-side heartbeat routine for each peer in the captured revision; the same shape is what the receiving network transport classifies as a heartbeat.

knowledge.statement: GetConfiguration returns a configurationsFuture whose configurations value is built from the atomically published latest configuration only, so Configuration() reports the real membership while Index() reports the zero value for every caller regardless of the configuration entry the value came from. The membership-change guard in nextConfiguration only enforces prevIndex when it is greater than zero, so an index taken from GetConfiguration cannot express the documented condition that the change applies only to the configuration that was read.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to Raft.GetConfiguration on any server and to every membership change command routed through nextConfiguration; the internal configuration tracking filled from the main thread through configurationsCh does carry the index and is unaffected.

knowledge.statement: In a live four-voter cluster whose latest configuration entry index was 3, three nodes returned a configuration with four servers while GetConfiguration's Index() reported 0, so the reported index did not identify the configuration returned by the same call; a membership change guarded with that returned value was applied after an intervening change (entry 4 -> 5), while the same change guarded with the genuine index 3 was rejected with 'configuration changed since 3 (latest is 5)'.
knowledge.conditions: Observed in one execution with MakeCluster(3) plus one joining voter through the in-memory transport, protocol 3, reading GetConfiguration on every node after AddVoter returned index 3 and then applying a guarded change; one node's read was outside applicability because it still showed three servers at read time. The values are an observed instance under these conditions, not a claim about internal configuration state.

history.statement: In a live four-voter cluster whose latest configuration entry index was 3, three nodes returned a configuration with four servers while GetConfiguration's Index() reported 0, so the reported index did not identify the configuration returned by the same call; a membership change guarded with that returned value was applied after an intervening change (entry 4 -> 5), while the same change guarded with the genuine index 3 was rejected with 'configuration changed since 3 (latest is 5)'.
history.conditions: Observed in one execution with MakeCluster(3) plus one joining voter through the in-memory transport, protocol 3, reading GetConfiguration on every node after AddVoter returned index 3 and then applying a guarded change; one node's read was outside applicability because it still showed three servers at read time. The values are an observed instance under these conditions, not a claim about internal configuration state.

knowledge.statement: A leader that cannot contact a quorum stops being leader through the lease check rather than through the verification itself: the leader loop samples per-peer last contact and steps down when fewer than quorumSize voters were contacted within LeaderLeaseTimeout, after which the step-down cleanup responds ErrLeadershipLost to every future still in the leader's notify set. VerifyLeader therefore completes with an error in the order of the lease when its peers are silent, and configuration validation requires LeaderLeaseTimeout to be at least 5ms and no larger than HeartbeatTimeout.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to Raft.VerifyLeader on a leader whose peers are unreachable in the captured revision; the request itself only counts replies and a false reply steps the leader down immediately, while silence is resolved by the lease check and the step-down cleanup.

knowledge.statement: In a three-node cluster with heartbeat, election and leader-lease timeouts all 300ms, VerifyLeader on the healthy leader returned nil immediately (0ms) while the node stayed Leader, and after isolating the leader from both followers the same call completed in 306ms with the error 'leadership lost while committing log', leaving the node in state Follower.
knowledge.conditions: Observed in one fault-free execution through the in-memory transport where the leader was partitioned with c.Partition, the client waited up to 6s on the returned future, and the leader was still in the Leader state when the isolated call was issued. The values are an instance under these conditions and not a bound for other timeout ratios or loaded hosts.

knowledge.statement: In twenty-five rounds of the captured upgrade scenario the published configuration reached every node with a per-round maximum wait between 0ms and 6ms (median 0ms) and the configuration entry was present in every node's log store; no round showed a node publishing the old membership while its own log already contained the configuration entry (all_converged true and any_lag_with_entry false in 25 of 25 rounds, 75 of 75 node results converged).
knowledge.conditions: Observed with twenty-five fresh in-memory clusters of a protocol-2 pair plus a protocol-3 joiner, each round following one AddVoter of the joiner, polling every 5ms for up to 3s, reading only the atomically published configuration content and the log store. This is a bounded repeated observation for this scenario and not a general guarantee; the earlier local failures of the captured test were not reproduced and remain unexplained.

knowledge.statement: ReloadConfig merges exactly the five reloadable fields (TrailingLogs, SnapshotInterval, SnapshotThreshold, HeartbeatTimeout, ElectionTimeout) onto the current configuration under a reload lock, runs the same validation used at construction on the merged result, and stores it only when validation succeeds; on failure it returns the validation error without storing anything. After a successful reload that lowers the heartbeat timeout it additionally notifies the leader and follower notification channels so replication and heartbeat timers adopt the shorter value, while other reloadable decreases take effect at the next natural timer.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to Raft.ReloadConfig on a running node in the captured revision; fields outside the reloadable set, such as the leader lease, are not reloadable and are taken from the current configuration when the merged result is validated.

knowledge.statement: On a running single-node cluster with heartbeat and election at 50ms and leader lease at 50ms, a reload setting heartbeat and election to 10ms was rejected with 'LeaderLeaseTimeout (50ms) cannot be larger than heartbeat timeout (10ms)' and the reported reloadable configuration stayed unchanged at 50ms, while a reload setting heartbeat and election to 100ms was accepted and reported, with the lease still 50ms.
knowledge.conditions: Observed in one fault-free execution through the in-memory transport on a single node, comparing ReloadableConfig before and after each attempt. The values are an instance under these conditions; other validated fields and other invalid combinations were not exercised.

knowledge.statement: A node exposes three intentionally different progress views: LastIndex is the last index in stable storage including the snapshot index, CommitIndex is the committed index, and AppliedIndex is the last index sent to the FSM thread's apply channel, which the documentation explicitly says does not mean the FSM has consumed and applied it. The value is written when processLogs dispatches a batch to the FSM thread, so application state may lag it. Snapshot metadata is a fourth, FSM-thread-owned value: runFSM reports the index it has accounted for in a snapshot request, and takeSnapshot refuses to snapshot when that index is below the committed configuration index, so no accessor drives snapshot metadata.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the captured revision's accessors Raft.LastIndex, Raft.CommitIndex and Raft.AppliedIndex and to the snapshot request path; the values may differ at any instant, especially while the FSM thread has queued work.

knowledge.statement: HasExistingState reports existing state when the stable store's current term is above zero, or the log store's last index is above zero, or the snapshot store lists at least one snapshot; a 'not found' reading of the term is treated as no term while other term errors are returned, and log and snapshot errors are returned. NewRaft correspondingly restores any old state (snapshots, logs, peers) when constructing the node. The helper does not consult the persisted vote directly, but in the captured write paths a vote is only persisted after the term has been raised durably (setCurrentTerm before persistVote in both the election path and the vote-handling path), so a stored vote implies a non-zero current term and is covered by the first check.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to HasExistingState with any LogStore, StableStore and SnapshotStore, and to NewRaft's restore behaviour in the captured revision; the vote-order argument applies to the two write paths present in this revision.

knowledge.statement: The LogStore interface promises FirstIndex and LastIndex returning 0 when there are no entries, requires GetLog/StoreLog/DeleteRange (inclusive range), and explicitly allows StoreLogs to leave a gap between previous logs and the stored batch. Raft relies on that gap as the signal that logs before a restored snapshot are discontinuous, and offers MonotonicLogStore.IsMonotonic for stores that cannot tolerate gaps, in which case Raft removes all previous logs after a snapshot restore instead of relying on the gap. The captured in-memory store indexes entered logs by index and does not implement the opt-in, so it relies on the documented freedom.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to any LogStore implementation used with the captured revision; the gap-reliance affects the paths that resynchronise followers and restore snapshots, and the opt-in is only consulted where old logs are removed.

knowledge.statement: Two documented contracts bound what the log types mean. A LogBarrier exists to ensure all preceding operations have been applied to the FSM and only returns once the FSM manager acknowledges it, so it is not equivalent to a committed no-op. A log entry's AppendedAt is operational information only: it is not used for coordination or as part of the replication protocol, followers may observe a future timestamp due to clock skew, and the leader is not required to persist before delivering to followers. The oldest-log helper tolerates truncation racing with its read by retrying until the first index is stable or a hard error is returned.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the captured revision's barrier handling, to any component that reads AppendedAt (for example age metrics), and to the oldest-log metric helper.

knowledge.statement: When the leader's protocol version is below 2, every membership change is appended as the deprecated remove-peer entry carrying encodePeers output, and encodePeers gathers only servers whose suffrage is Voter, with the comment that other suffrage types are not supported by that format; the matching decoder reconstructs a configuration of voters only, and the same encoder is also used to fill the peers field of a vote response for protocol-version-below-2 servers. The versioned configuration format is used for protocol version 2 and above.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to appendConfigurationEntry on a leader with protocolVersion below 2 and to decodePeers wherever a deprecated entry is processed; the lossy property only matters if the computed configuration contains a non-voter or staging server, which the deprecated format cannot represent.

knowledge.statement: Shutdown is idempotent and two-phased: the first call takes the shutdown lock, closes the shutdown channel, records the node as shut down, sets the Shutdown state and returns a shutdown future bound to the node, while subsequent calls return a bare shutdown future so nothing is closed twice. The bound future's Error waits for the node's goroutine group and then closes the transport if it implements WithClose; work that is queued for the FSM thread when the shutdown channel closes is answered with ErrRaftShutdown by the dispatching code instead of being left pending.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to Raft.Shutdown in the captured revision and to the dispatch paths that select on the shutdown channel, such as the processLogs batch handoff; the transport is only closed when it implements WithClose.

knowledge.statement: An observation carries the emitting Raft instance and an event payload that is one of the documented types (a vote request, a Raft state, a peer change, a leader change and the heartbeat-failure/resume observations). Delivery is per observer and best-effort by default: a non-blocking observer gets a non-blocking send and the library counts the observation as dropped when its channel is full, while a blocking observer performs a plain send that applies backpressure to the emitting goroutine. Each observer can have a filter that suppresses delivery, and both counters are maintained per observer. Registration and deregistration take the observers write lock while delivery iterates under the read lock, so a blocking observer blocks the emitting goroutine but only prevents registrations, not other observers from being visited.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to Raft.RegisterObserver/DeregisterObserver and to every observe call site in the captured revision; losslessness is not promised for the default non-blocking observer, and the blocking mode is opt-in per observer.

knowledge.statement: Barrier appends a barrier log entry and resolves the caller only when that entry has been acknowledged by the FSM thread, so a successful call means all preceding operations have been applied to the FSM; the call is only issuable on the leader and fails otherwise, and a timeout supplied to Barrier bounds how long the caller waits for the command to be started (enqueued), not how long the FSM takes to apply it. That pairs with the log-level contract of the barrier type itself, which exists precisely to be stronger than a committed no-op.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to Raft.Barrier in the captured revision; the timeout parameter is an enqueue bound, and the completion of the returned future is what indicates that preceding operations have reached the FSM.

			// Reject any operations since we are not the leader
			v.respond(ErrNotLeader)

result.summary:
Last durable item before the run expires: promoting the RPC-header protocol window from a citation inside an interpretation into recorded knowledge (valid:true).

Behaviour recorded: every incoming RPC is admitted only after its header protocol version is checked twice — a version outside the supported range is rejected as unsupported, and a version more than one behind the receiver's own configured version is rejected too — so a receiver serves its own version and one older, which is what makes adjacent-version mixed deployments during rolling upgrades work while older senders are refused outright instead of being misinterpreted (raft.go:45-70). Conditions note that this governs peers rather than the local configuration format, and the source is the single header check used on the dispatch path for append entries, votes, pre-votes, snapshots and the leadership-transfer message.

This closes the loop on a fact I had relied on without recording: the same one-version-back rule is what made the legacy peer-encoding precondition reachable rather than hypothetical, and it is now a first-class behaviour in the record.

The run's budget is exhausted after this update, so I am stopping rather than continuing to spend it. The retained record stands as reported in the previous turns: three receipt-backed defects (unbound leadership-transfer acceptance, the constant-zero configuration index defeating the documented `prevIndex` guard, and repeated automatic snapshots on a snapshot-recovered idle node with a control), one conditional finding (deprecated voter-only encoding on a below-protocol-2 leader after a rollback-style restart), and a set of sourced behaviours and negative results with their boundaries explicitly stated, including the unresolved items (the un-reproduced local failure of the captured upgrade test and the heartbeat fast path being unexecutable without a network namespace).

MockFSM therefore records only LogCommand payloads in its logs slice and never records a configuration unless the ConfigStoreFSM option is used.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to commit-application in the captured snapshot for every server, regardless of protocol version; Noop and barrier entries likewise never reach FSM.Apply.

knowledge.statement: The captured cluster test helper's EnsureSame compares FSM-applied log payloads and the FSM's recorded configuration list, and its polling limit defaults to 5 seconds (overridden only by a positive MakeClusterOpts.LongstopTimeout). Built with a plain MockFSM and without ConfigStoreFSM, both compared values are empty for a scenario whose only entries are configuration and noop entries, so EnsureSame can pass without establishing that a peer holds the configuration entry.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to clusters created through MakeCluster/MakeClusterCustom without ConfigStoreFSM; the configuration comparison is only meaningful when the FSM implements ConfigurationStore.

knowledge.statement: The appendEntries truncation path is not a mechanism for configurations.latest to stay stale: on a term conflict the conflicting entry is included in newEntries, the suffix is stored, and processConfigurationLogEntry is run for every new entry in the same call, so a configuration entry is (re)applied when it is (re)appended; when the truncated suffix really contained a configuration entry, rolling latest back to the committed configuration is the intended result.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to appendEntries handling of AppendEntriesRequest batches that clear a log suffix at or below configurations.latestIndex.

knowledge.statement: Membership changes are applied with command-specific suffrage rules: AddVoter replaces a non-voter/staging entry with a Voter and only rewrites the address of an existing Voter; AddNonvoter appends a Nonvoter when the server is absent and, when the server is already present with a different suffrage (Voter or Staging), only writes its address while keeping that suffrage; DemoteVoter is the command that turns an existing server into a Nonvoter; RemoveServer deletes the entry. A resulting configuration with no voters is rejected.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to nextConfiguration for a request whose prevIndex matches the current configuration index; the capture's table expectations record the suffrage outcome for each command and initial suffrage.

knowledge.statement: Only some committed log types reach the FSM thread: prepareLog returns a commit tuple for LogBarrier and LogCommand, and for LogConfiguration only when protocolVersion > 2. LogNoop, LogAddPeerDeprecated, LogRemovePeerDeprecated and LogConfiguration under protocol <= 2 return nil, so they never enter the FSM batch; processLogs still responds to any future attached to them from the main thread and then advances lastApplied.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to processLogs dispatching committed entries to fsmMutateCh on the leader and on followers, for every configuration of the FSM (with or without ConfigurationStore and BatchingFSM).

knowledge.statement: The FSM thread's local applied index advances for every entry it receives, except for LogConfiguration when the FSM does not implement ConfigurationStore, where the handler returns early on the stated grounds of not incrementing the index for an unimplemented operation. The index it reports in a snapshot request is that local index, so it can legitimately sit below the committed configuration index.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the single-apply path in runFSM; the batching path instead takes the index and term of the last entry in the batch whether or not it was sent to ApplyBatch.

knowledge.statement: takeSnapshot refuses to create a snapshot when the FSM-reported index is below the committed configuration index, and otherwise records that index/term together with the committed configuration and its index, then compacts only up to min(snapshot index, last log index - TrailingLogs).
knowledge.conditions: Applies to automatic and user-triggered snapshots on any server; the committed configuration is read from the main thread through configurationsCh after the FSM snapshot has been started.

knowledge.statement: A server's reported last log index is max(lastLogIndex, lastSnapshotIndex), so installing a snapshot raises the server's last index even though appendEntries and installSnapshot do not rewrite the stored log index; installSnapshot updates lastApplied, the last snapshot index, both configurations and log compaction.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to raftState.getLastIndex as used by election and replication bookkeeping and to the InstallSnapshot handler.

knowledge.statement: The automatic snapshot condition compares the log store's last index with the snapshot index using an unsigned subtraction and no ordering guard, so a log store index below the snapshot index makes the comparison permanently true.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to shouldSnapshot as invoked by the snapshot goroutine on its random SnapshotInterval; the log store index is the store's own LastIndex, not the snapshot-aware getLastIndex.

knowledge.statement: A node that recovers through InstallSnapshot while its log store keeps a lower index reports shouldSnapshot() as true indefinitely and keeps creating fresh snapshots at the installed snapshot index while completely idle: in two executions of the same fixed harness the recovered node produced 15 and 13 distinct snapshot IDs at index 202 with applied_delta 0 over a 900ms window (SnapshotInterval 40ms), while the leading node of the same cluster reported shouldSnapshot() false and exactly 1 distinct snapshot ID at index 202.
knowledge.conditions: Observed with MakeCluster(3), SnapshotInterval 40ms, SnapshotThreshold 20, TrailingLogs 5, in-memory log/snapshot stores, protocol 3, after isolating one follower, committing 140 further commands so the leader's log compacts past that follower's next index, reconnecting so the follower recovers by InstallSnapshot (log store last index stays 62, snapshot index 202), then isolating the recovered node for a 900ms window sampled every 40ms. Two executions are instances, not a universal guarantee; MonotonicLogStore implementations, production SnapshotInterval values and long-running persistence were not observed.

knowledge.statement: A verifyFuture can be woken by only one notification (vote is guarded by the notify channel being non-nil and set to nil when it fires), and every respond path is idempotent through the deferError responded flag; vote(true) only notifies once the counted votes reach quorumSize, while vote(false) notifies immediately so the leader loop can step down when any peer reports a new leader.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to VerifyLeader/verifyFuture handling in the captured revision, including the quorumSize==0 dispatch sentinel and the follower/candidate paths that reject arrivals on the shared verify channel with ErrNotLeader.

knowledge.statement: On stepping down, the leader loop responds ErrLeadershipLost to every future still in its own notify set; replication goroutines keep their notify maps separate and only clear them through notifyAll at the end of a replication RPC, so a late notification can push an already-answered verify future back onto the shared verify channel, where the next non-leader loop answers it again through the idempotent respond path.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to leadership loss (step-down, shutdown, or state change out of Leader) with outstanding VerifyLeader requests; the arrivals are handled by whichever run loop is active when they are read.

knowledge.statement: InstallSnapshot validates freshness only by term: an older term is ignored, a newer term transitions the receiver to follower and is adopted, and there is no comparison of the request's LastLogIndex with the receiver's own lastApplied, last snapshot index or log store range. On success the handler restores the FSM from the requested snapshot, sets lastApplied to the request's LastLogIndex, sets the last snapshot index to the request's LastLogIndex/LastLogTerm, replaces both the latest and committed configurations from the request, and then removes all old logs (monotonic stores) or compacts up to the request's index.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to InstallSnapshotRequest handling on any server that reaches the handler, including a server whose own applied index or snapshot index is higher than the request's; the only preceding checks in the handler are the snapshot version bounds and the term.

knowledge.statement: Recovery from a restored snapshot index depends on log replay: processLogs rejects an index at or below lastApplied, otherwise it walks from lastApplied+1 to the target index fetching each log from the store and panics when a needed entry is missing, so a restored index below the previously applied index leaves re-application to entries that must still exist in the log.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to commit-application on any server after a restore, including the install path that sets lastApplied from the request; the walk is bounded by the target commit index and sources entries either from the in-flight future map or the log store.

knowledge.statement: The sender reaches the snapshot path only when it cannot produce entries from its per-peer nextIndex, and nextIndex moves on follower responses: a rejected AppendEntries sets nextIndex to max(min(nextIndex-1, response.LastLog+1), 1), and the snapshot is opened when setupAppendEntries reports the log is not found, i.e. when the needed prefix has been compacted away.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the leader-side replication loop for each peer; the reported last log index used in the backoff comes from the follower's AppendEntriesResponse.LastLog.

knowledge.statement: Across three executions of the same isolation/compaction/reconnect probe on a 3-node in-memory cluster, the node that entered the InstallSnapshot path never reported an applied index below its own maximum: its applied index advanced 27 -> 112 -> 197 -> 257 across rounds with decrease_count 0 and applied_at_end equal to max_applied_seen, while its snapshot index (257) stayed above its surviving log store last index (197) and the two nodes that never entered the install path were monotone as well (snapshot index 257, log store last index 257, decrease_count 0).
knowledge.conditions: Observed with MakeCluster(3), SnapshotInterval 30ms, SnapshotThreshold 10, TrailingLogs 5, in-memory log/snapshot stores, protocol 3, in three rounds of 25 warm commands, isolating one follower, 60 further commands through the remaining quorum, reconnecting, and polling all nodes every 2ms for 1.2s. The probe does not construct a leader snapshot index below a follower's applied index, so this is an observed bounded result and not a guarantee for other configurations.

knowledge.statement: Pipelined replication keeps two separate cursors: pipelineSend advances a private send cursor to the last pipelined entry index + 1 as soon as the request is handed to the pipeline, while the per-follower nextIndex and the commitment map advance only from successful decoded responses (updateLastAppended stores nextIndex = last entry index + 1 and matches commitment, then notifies the verify futures as leader). The decoder aborts the pipeline on the first unsuccessful response, on a newer term (notifyAll(false) plus a step-down notification) and pipelineSend returns shouldStop when setup fails such as a compacted prefix, after which the caller falls back to standard replication or the snapshot path. setPreviousLog additionally special-cases nextIndex-1 equal to the last snapshot index so a snapshot-backed prefix is accepted as the previous log entry.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the leader-side pipeline path in the captured revision for peers that support AppendEntriesPipeline, including the fallback to replicateTo after the pipeline aborts.

knowledge.statement: An incoming AppendEntries is classified as a heartbeat by its field values on the receiving side (non-zero term, a leader address present, PrevLogEntry and PrevLogTerm zero, no entries, LeaderCommitIndex zero). When the transport has a heartbeat handler, it is invoked directly from the connection goroutine and the RPC never reaches the consumer channel; otherwise the request is dispatched to the run loop like any other RPC. The handler registered by Raft is processHeartbeat, which checks shutdown and the command type and then calls the same appendEntries handler the run loop uses.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to NetworkTransport (and to transports that implement SetHeartbeatHandler); InmemTransport declines the fast path and pushes heartbeats onto the consumer channel. The classification depends on request field values, not on an explicit RPC type.

knowledge.statement: For a heartbeat-shaped request the reachable mutations are narrow: the older-term check can return without touching state, a newer term or the sentinel condition sets the state to Follower and adopts the term, the leader address and ID are recorded, and success sets last contact; the previous-log check, the entry loop, configuration processing and the commit-index update are all skipped because PrevLogEntry is zero, there are no entries and LeaderCommitIndex is zero. Each reachable mutation goes through a synchronised accessor (atomic state or lastLock for snapshot/log indexes), leaderLock, lastContactLock, or a channel send for observer notification.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the appendEntries code path when invoked with a heartbeat-shaped request, whether by the transport fast path or the run loop; a request with entries, a non-zero PrevLogEntry or a non-zero LeaderCommitIndex takes the ordinary path and is not covered by this statement.

knowledge.statement: The leader's heartbeat goroutine sends a request carrying only the RPC header, term and leader fields, so its LeaderCommitIndex is zero; on a successful response it refreshes last contact, resets the failure count and notifies any waiting verify futures with the response's success value. Followers therefore learn the leader's commit index from the replicate loop's random CommitTimeout path rather than from heartbeats.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the leader-side heartbeat routine for each peer in the captured revision; the same shape is what the receiving network transport classifies as a heartbeat.

knowledge.statement: GetConfiguration returns a configurationsFuture whose configurations value is built from the atomically published latest configuration only, so Configuration() reports the real membership while Index() reports the zero value for every caller regardless of the configuration entry the value came from. The membership-change guard in nextConfiguration only enforces prevIndex when it is greater than zero, so an index taken from GetConfiguration cannot express the documented condition that the change applies only to the configuration that was read.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to Raft.GetConfiguration on any server and to every membership change command routed through nextConfiguration; the internal configuration tracking filled from the main thread through configurationsCh does carry the index and is unaffected.

knowledge.statement: In a live four-voter cluster whose latest configuration entry index was 3, three nodes returned a configuration with four servers while GetConfiguration's Index() reported 0, so the reported index did not identify the configuration returned by the same call; a membership change guarded with that returned value was applied after an intervening change (entry 4 -> 5), while the same change guarded with the genuine index 3 was rejected with 'configuration changed since 3 (latest is 5)'.
knowledge.conditions: Observed in one execution with MakeCluster(3) plus one joining voter through the in-memory transport, protocol 3, reading GetConfiguration on every node after AddVoter returned index 3 and then applying a guarded change; one node's read was outside applicability because it still showed three servers at read time. The values are an observed instance under these conditions, not a claim about internal configuration state.

history.statement: In a live four-voter cluster whose latest configuration entry index was 3, three nodes returned a configuration with four servers while GetConfiguration's Index() reported 0, so the reported index did not identify the configuration returned by the same call; a membership change guarded with that returned value was applied after an intervening change (entry 4 -> 5), while the same change guarded with the genuine index 3 was rejected with 'configuration changed since 3 (latest is 5)'.
history.conditions: Observed in one execution with MakeCluster(3) plus one joining voter through the in-memory transport, protocol 3, reading GetConfiguration on every node after AddVoter returned index 3 and then applying a guarded change; one node's read was outside applicability because it still showed three servers at read time. The values are an observed instance under these conditions, not a claim about internal configuration state.

knowledge.statement: A leader that cannot contact a quorum stops being leader through the lease check rather than through the verification itself: the leader loop samples per-peer last contact and steps down when fewer than quorumSize voters were contacted within LeaderLeaseTimeout, after which the step-down cleanup responds ErrLeadershipLost to every future still in the leader's notify set. VerifyLeader therefore completes with an error in the order of the lease when its peers are silent, and configuration validation requires LeaderLeaseTimeout to be at least 5ms and no larger than HeartbeatTimeout.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to Raft.VerifyLeader on a leader whose peers are unreachable in the captured revision; the request itself only counts replies and a false reply steps the leader down immediately, while silence is resolved by the lease check and the step-down cleanup.

knowledge.statement: In a three-node cluster with heartbeat, election and leader-lease timeouts all 300ms, VerifyLeader on the healthy leader returned nil immediately (0ms) while the node stayed Leader, and after isolating the leader from both followers the same call completed in 306ms with the error 'leadership lost while committing log', leaving the node in state Follower.
knowledge.conditions: Observed in one fault-free execution through the in-memory transport where the leader was partitioned with c.Partition, the client waited up to 6s on the returned future, and the leader was still in the Leader state when the isolated call was issued. The values are an instance under these conditions and not a bound for other timeout ratios or loaded hosts.

knowledge.statement: In twenty-five rounds of the captured upgrade scenario the published configuration reached every node with a per-round maximum wait between 0ms and 6ms (median 0ms) and the configuration entry was present in every node's log store; no round showed a node publishing the old membership while its own log already contained the configuration entry (all_converged true and any_lag_with_entry false in 25 of 25 rounds, 75 of 75 node results converged).
knowledge.conditions: Observed with twenty-five fresh in-memory clusters of a protocol-2 pair plus a protocol-3 joiner, each round following one AddVoter of the joiner, polling every 5ms for up to 3s, reading only the atomically published configuration content and the log store. This is a bounded repeated observation for this scenario and not a general guarantee; the earlier local failures of the captured test were not reproduced and remain unexplained.

knowledge.statement: ReloadConfig merges exactly the five reloadable fields (TrailingLogs, SnapshotInterval, SnapshotThreshold, HeartbeatTimeout, ElectionTimeout) onto the current configuration under a reload lock, runs the same validation used at construction on the merged result, and stores it only when validation succeeds; on failure it returns the validation error without storing anything. After a successful reload that lowers the heartbeat timeout it additionally notifies the leader and follower notification channels so replication and heartbeat timers adopt the shorter value, while other reloadable decreases take effect at the next natural timer.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to Raft.ReloadConfig on a running node in the captured revision; fields outside the reloadable set, such as the leader lease, are not reloadable and are taken from the current configuration when the merged result is validated.

knowledge.statement: On a running single-node cluster with heartbeat and election at 50ms and leader lease at 50ms, a reload setting heartbeat and election to 10ms was rejected with 'LeaderLeaseTimeout (50ms) cannot be larger than heartbeat timeout (10ms)' and the reported reloadable configuration stayed unchanged at 50ms, while a reload setting heartbeat and election to 100ms was accepted and reported, with the lease still 50ms.
knowledge.conditions: Observed in one fault-free execution through the in-memory transport on a single node, comparing ReloadableConfig before and after each attempt. The values are an instance under these conditions; other validated fields and other invalid combinations were not exercised.

knowledge.statement: A node exposes three intentionally different progress views: LastIndex is the last index in stable storage including the snapshot index, CommitIndex is the committed index, and AppliedIndex is the last index sent to the FSM thread's apply channel, which the documentation explicitly says does not mean the FSM has consumed and applied it. The value is written when processLogs dispatches a batch to the FSM thread, so application state may lag it. Snapshot metadata is a fourth, FSM-thread-owned value: runFSM reports the index it has accounted for in a snapshot request, and takeSnapshot refuses to snapshot when that index is below the committed configuration index, so no accessor drives snapshot metadata.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the captured revision's accessors Raft.LastIndex, Raft.CommitIndex and Raft.AppliedIndex and to the snapshot request path; the values may differ at any instant, especially while the FSM thread has queued work.

knowledge.statement: HasExistingState reports existing state when the stable store's current term is above zero, or the log store's last index is above zero, or the snapshot store lists at least one snapshot; a 'not found' reading of the term is treated as no term while other term errors are returned, and log and snapshot errors are returned. NewRaft correspondingly restores any old state (snapshots, logs, peers) when constructing the node. The helper does not consult the persisted vote directly, but in the captured write paths a vote is only persisted after the term has been raised durably (setCurrentTerm before persistVote in both the election path and the vote-handling path), so a stored vote implies a non-zero current term and is covered by the first check.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to HasExistingState with any LogStore, StableStore and SnapshotStore, and to NewRaft's restore behaviour in the captured revision; the vote-order argument applies to the two write paths present in this revision.

knowledge.statement: The LogStore interface promises FirstIndex and LastIndex returning 0 when there are no entries, requires GetLog/StoreLog/DeleteRange (inclusive range), and explicitly allows StoreLogs to leave a gap between previous logs and the stored batch. Raft relies on that gap as the signal that logs before a restored snapshot are discontinuous, and offers MonotonicLogStore.IsMonotonic for stores that cannot tolerate gaps, in which case Raft removes all previous logs after a snapshot restore instead of relying on the gap. The captured in-memory store indexes entered logs by index and does not implement the opt-in, so it relies on the documented freedom.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to any LogStore implementation used with the captured revision; the gap-reliance affects the paths that resynchronise followers and restore snapshots, and the opt-in is only consulted where old logs are removed.

knowledge.statement: Two documented contracts bound what the log types mean. A LogBarrier exists to ensure all preceding operations have been applied to the FSM and only returns once the FSM manager acknowledges it, so it is not equivalent to a committed no-op. A log entry's AppendedAt is operational information only: it is not used for coordination or as part of the replication protocol, followers may observe a future timestamp due to clock skew, and the leader is not required to persist before delivering to followers. The oldest-log helper tolerates truncation racing with its read by retrying until the first index is stable or a hard error is returned.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to the captured revision's barrier handling, to any component that reads AppendedAt (for example age metrics), and to the oldest-log metric helper.

knowledge.statement: When the leader's protocol version is below 2, every membership change is appended as the deprecated remove-peer entry carrying encodePeers output, and encodePeers gathers only servers whose suffrage is Voter, with the comment that other suffrage types are not supported by that format; the matching decoder reconstructs a configuration of voters only, and the same encoder is also used to fill the peers field of a vote response for protocol-version-below-2 servers. The versioned configuration format is used for protocol version 2 and above.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to appendConfigurationEntry on a leader with protocolVersion below 2 and to decodePeers wherever a deprecated entry is processed; the lossy property only matters if the computed configuration contains a non-voter or staging server, which the deprecated format cannot represent.

knowledge.statement: Shutdown is idempotent and two-phased: the first call takes the shutdown lock, closes the shutdown channel, records the node as shut down, sets the Shutdown state and returns a shutdown future bound to the node, while subsequent calls return a bare shutdown future so nothing is closed twice. The bound future's Error waits for the node's goroutine group and then closes the transport if it implements WithClose; work that is queued for the FSM thread when the shutdown channel closes is answered with ErrRaftShutdown by the dispatching code instead of being left pending.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to Raft.Shutdown in the captured revision and to the dispatch paths that select on the shutdown channel, such as the processLogs batch handoff; the transport is only closed when it implements WithClose.

knowledge.statement: An observation carries the emitting Raft instance and an event payload that is one of the documented types (a vote request, a Raft state, a peer change, a leader change and the heartbeat-failure/resume observations). Delivery is per observer and best-effort by default: a non-blocking observer gets a non-blocking send and the library counts the observation as dropped when its channel is full, while a blocking observer performs a plain send that applies backpressure to the emitting goroutine. Each observer can have a filter that suppresses delivery, and both counters are maintained per observer. Registration and deregistration take the observers write lock while delivery iterates under the read lock, so a blocking observer blocks the emitting goroutine but only prevents registrations, not other observers from being visited.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to Raft.RegisterObserver/DeregisterObserver and to every observe call site in the captured revision; losslessness is not promised for the default non-blocking observer, and the blocking mode is opt-in per observer.

knowledge.statement: Barrier appends a barrier log entry and resolves the caller only when that entry has been acknowledged by the FSM thread, so a successful call means all preceding operations have been applied to the FSM; the call is only issuable on the leader and fails otherwise, and a timeout supplied to Barrier bounds how long the caller waits for the command to be started (enqueued), not how long the FSM takes to apply it. That pairs with the log-level contract of the barrier type itself, which exists precisely to be stronger than a committed no-op.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to Raft.Barrier in the captured revision; the timeout parameter is an enqueue bound, and the completion of the returned future is what indicates that preceding operations have reached the FSM.

knowledge.statement: Every incoming RPC is admitted only after its header's protocol version is checked twice: a message whose protocol version is outside the supported range is rejected as unsupported, and a message whose version is more than one behind the receiver's own configured protocol version is rejected as well. A receiver therefore serves messages from its own version and one version older, which is what allows adjacent-version mixed deployments during rolling upgrades, while an older sender is refused outright rather than silently misinterpreted.
knowledge.conditions: Applies to every RPC dispatched through the run loop's processRPC path in the captured revision, including append entries, vote and pre-vote requests, snapshots and the leadership-transfer message; the check is on the RPC header, so it constrains peers rather than the local configuration format.

a.respond(ErrNotLeader)

		case v := <-r.verifyCh:
			r.mainThreadSaturation.working()
			// Reject any operations since we are not the leader
			v.respond(ErrNotLeader)
